panels.title: Invalid responses (10 min)

panels.description: Blocked while Discord's edge blocks this IP and Sluice pauses all outbound traffic. A refusal of one client, confirmed by Sluice's own probe to be only that client, does not count.
panels.title: Cloudflare block

panels.description: Edge refusals are responses from Discord's edge rather than Discord (a 429 or 403 without Via). Confirmed blocks are refusals that Sluice's own probe showed to cover this whole IP.
panels.title: Edge refusals and confirmed blocks

panels.description: How long requests waited for their bucket and the global limit before their first Discord attempt. A request that would wait longer than QUEUE_TIMEOUT gets a 429 instead.
panels.title: Queue wait p95 by route

panels.description: Requests Sluice answered with an error of its own, or abandoned, by reason. CONFIG.md lists what each reason means, and which of them are faults to act on.
panels.title: Proxy failures by reason

panels.description: Shared-scope 429s limit one resource and leave the bucket open; they do not count against the invalid-request budget. Edge statuses came from Discord's edge rather than Discord.
panels.title: Shared-scope and edge responses

panels.description: Calls to webhooks Discord reported as unknown (10015) or invalid (50027), answered by Sluice for an hour so they never reach Discord.
panels.title: Deleted-webhook calls answered by Sluice

panels.description: Requests naming a deprecated or discontinued Discord API version, or none, which Discord serves as its deprecated default, v6. Current versions are v9 and v10.
panels.title: Deprecated API versions

panels.description: How much of each limit on what Sluice holds at once is in use: client states, bearer tokens, buckets, requests in flight and the bytes kept for retries, each named after its MAX_ setting. A limit that is reached refuses requests, which Proxy failures by reason shows under the reasons ending in _limit.
panels.title: Limits in use

panels.description: Each bot's request rate against the requests a second Sluice paces it at. Interaction callbacks are left out, because Discord does not count them against the limit. So are Bearer, NoAuth and Other, which stand for many clients or for requests Sluice does not pace.
panels.title: Global limit in use, by bot

panels.description: Log lines at warning and at error level. When either moves, the log says what needs attention.
